name: Blacklisted
label: Deathwish
lede: [[George Hirsch]] kept quitting Blacklisted and kept coming back. The Philadelphia band tunes down to C and rarely runs past twenty minutes a record.

eras.title: A Philly band lands on Deathwish
eras.text: Blacklisted start in Philadelphia in 2003. By 2005 a split with First Blood has put them on Deathwish Inc., and a first full-length is in the racks.

years.p: The first releases are a self-titled 7-inch and the Our Youth Is Wasted EP on Stillborn.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia the original line-up was Hirsch on vocals, Jon Nean and Tim Smith on guitar and bass, and Zach Trotta on drums. Later interviews describe Smith as the main songwriter and Trotta as the drummer he replaced on the first album.

years.h: A split with First Blood puts Blacklisted in front of Deathwish
years.p: Dead Man's Hand: 3 is how [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s label first hears the band.
years.xp:
Hirsch told No Echo that Deathwish head Bannon (the source calls him Jake) showed interest after the split, and "some stuff got worked out from there." The whole Deathwish crew then came to the studio to see the band and were supportive.

Deathwish lists the release as Dead Man's Hand: 3.

years.h: ...The Beat Goes On runs 13 songs in about 24 minutes
years.p: Engineer Jim Seigel records Blacklisted's first Deathwish full-length in bursts of two or three weeks between tours.
years.xp:
Tim Smith and Shawn Foley wrote the music together in a jam room over a few weeks, and the band tuned down to C. Hirsch told No Echo he hoped to land in "that dark murky sound that I loved from death metal, but still be just hardcore." He took cues from Turmoil and Buried Alive.

Hirsch also said he was at first unhappy with the record, and "too selfish and wrapped up in my own part" to see how much weight Smith and Foley carried.

eras.title: Heavier than heaven
eras.text: Tim Smith leaves and the band nearly folds. Then comes a 19-minute album with Kurt Ballou, and a follow-up with a violin on it.

years.h: Tim Smith leaves, and Blacklisted nearly go with him
years.p: Hirsch told Scene Point Blank the band came close to ending in 2006 after losing a key songwriter.
years.xp: The band carried on with Hirsch, Shawn Foley, Dave Walling and a rotating guitar slot. In later interviews Hirsch said he has quit the band many times to sort things out.

years.h: Peace on Earth, War on Stage is over in six minutes
years.p: Four songs on a 7-inch for Deathwish (DWI58), pressed in 3,000 copies according to Wikipedia. Two of them get re-recorded for the next album.
play: Peace on Earth, War on Stage

years.cap: Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God, Deathwish DWI70
years.src: Wikipedia · No Echo · Scene Point Blank
years.h: Kurt Ballou produces Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God
years.p: Eleven songs in 19 minutes 37 seconds. [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] produces and Alan Douches masters.
years.xp:
Fans and reviewers most often point to this as Blacklisted's best record. No Echo calls it one of the best hardcore releases of its decade. Hirsch told Scene Point Blank the title nods to the name of Nirvana's first European tour.

The band planned tours of Australia, Mexico, Central and South America and Japan around it. Hirsch said he had toured into a Twilight Zone type of vortex.

years.cap: Blacklisted on a low, packed stage, June 2008
years.h: No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me brings in a violin
years.p: Will Yip records 14 songs (DWI100) with trumpet, rainstick and backing vocals from Melissa Farley.
years.xp: Hirsch later called it the band's most definitive record in a Punknews interview. The CD carried three bonus tracks from the Eccentrichine EP.
play: No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me

eras.title: Six years between albums
eras.text: Family and life slow Blacklisted down. Hirsch records folk under another name, gets through a hard year, and the band returns in 2015 with a fourth album.

years.cap: Blacklisted's drummer, This Is Hardcore, Philadelphia, August 2011
years.p: Six Feet Under releases the EP, and its three tracks ride along as bonus tracks on the CD of No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me.

years.cap: Hirsch singing with Blacklisted, This Is Hardcore, Philadelphia, August 2011
years.h: Hirsch goes acoustic as Harm Wülf
years.p: There's Honey In the Soil So We Wait for the Till... is dark folk, released in November while Blacklisted sit quiet.
years.xp: A second Harm Wülf record, Hijrah, followed in 2016 with cover art from a photograph Hirsch took of the Sólheimasandur plane wreck in Iceland. Hirsch has since released music as Rose Clouds and returned to hardcore with Staticlone.

years.h: Blacklisted go quiet while Hirsch struggles
years.p: Hirsch told Punknews in 2015 that the band paused the year before during a mental health crisis, and credited promoter Joe Hardcore for support.
years.xp: The same interview places Blacklisted at This Is Hardcore in August 2014 and mentions a European run through Iceland and Finland. Hirsch said he had quit the band about fifty times.

years.cap: Hirsch in the pit, Wrecking Ball, The Masquerade, Atlanta, August 2015
years.h: Six years after the last album, When People Grow, People Go
years.p: Will Yip produces 11 songs in just over 20 minutes. "Deeper Kind" streams in December 2014, and "Turn in the Pike" gets a video.
years.xp: Writing began in late 2013. Wikipedia describes the record as blending the band's experimental and hardcore sides after a 2012 EP.

years.cap: Blacklisted's singer in the crowd, Wrecking Ball, The Masquerade, Atlanta, August 2015
years.h: The 10th-anniversary shows turn out to be the last for five years
years.p: Blacklisted build the sets around Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God, then don't play again until 2023.

eras.title: Back for Unbroken
eras.text: After five quiet years, Blacklisted return for one basement show. The reason is a friend's request, not a comeback plan.

years.h: Unbroken announce Philadelphia, and Blacklisted are on the bill
years.p: Blacklisted are billed alongside the reunited Unbroken and Damnation A.D. at First Unitarian Church. Wikipedia says it sold out in under a minute and a second night was added.

q: The only reason we're here tonight is because Unbroken asked us.
yt: Full set, First Unitarian Church, October 27, 2023
years.h: Hirsch tells a sold-out church basement why Blacklisted are back
years.p: About 600 people hear Blacklisted open with "Tourist" from ...The Beat Goes On and cover Ink & Dagger's "Full Circle". Stereogum heard no rust after five years off.
years.xp:
Hirsch's first words, per Stereogum: "Cut the fucking lights, this band is called Blacklisted." Then, later: "The only reason we're here tonight is because Unbroken asked us. And how could we say 'no' when we always say 'no.'"

The set leaned on Heavier Than Heaven, Lonelier Than God, with songs from No One Deserves to Be Here More Than Me and When People Grow, People Go, and closed with "Wish". Entry and Damnation A.D. opened, and Unbroken closed the night.

years.h: Hirsch's voice turns up on records by Converge, Nails and others
years.p: He has contributed vocals or lyrics to tracks by [[Ceremony|c13da818-d566-4f2a-aaaf-1c68301ddc43]], [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Cold World, Defeater and Nails.
years.xp: Hirsch also fronts Staticlone. In No Echo's 2023 interview he said no new Blacklisted material was planned and that the band had no further tours in view.
